warnings: 'พื้นชั้น 2' is the elevated, enclosed main living floor (bedroom/bathroom); its beams use a plain 'B' prefix, distinct from the ground-level 'GB'-prefixed beams on S-04. Spec confirmed on S-11: B1/B2/B3/B3A/B3B = 150x400mm (B3/B3A/B3B share one section on S-11); B4/BST1 = 150x350mm.

B3A appears twice at two different physical locations sharing the same mark: once as the row-A beam segment A2-A3, and again as a separate horizontal beam at dummy row A' (y=2.40) spanning grid2-grid3, splitting that bay into an upper slab room (S1) and a lower precast-plank room (SP). Both are genuine distinct beam instances with the same printed mark — kept as two atomic entries, not merged, per the 'reuse the mark, keep the position atomic' convention used throughout this house.

Beam B3A at row A' bears on the vertical B2 beams at both its grid2 and grid3 ends (a T-junction into a continuous through-beam, not a grid/column intersection) — flagged bears_on_beam at both ends rather than splitting B2.

'CS' point markers at row C (grid3, grid4) are steel square-tube posts (□-100x100x3.2mm per the legend on S-06/หน้า24, ขนาด confirmed there) — not RC columns; recorded as element_type 'column' with material 'steel' and a steel_section object, since the schema has no dedicated 'post' type and this member functions as a vertical support.
Grid3's vertical member changes mark from B2 (A-B span) to BST1 (B-C span) at row B — a stair-opening edge beam per S-12 (บันได ST1); BST1's spec (150x350mm) confirmed on S-11.

The row-C beam (B4, grid3-4) and both CS posts sit directly above the S-04 bay that has no footing/column at C1/C1' — architecturally this is the balcony over the open ground floor below, consistent with the balcony visible in the cover render (p.1).
